name: Claudianus
bio: Claudianus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors dates the poet to Byzantine period. Paton's index describes him as a Byzantine poet.
This archive carries the 4 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the third volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book IX: 139, 140, 753, 754).

poems.title: Book IX, 139
poems.author: Claudianus
poems.text: The wanton, accompanying her dance with shrill shrieks and castanets, beats the brazen clappers together with quivering movements. Her grey hair, the harbinger of death, is concealed by... She tortures her eyes to dart ineffectual flashes ; her false colour is sicklied o’er by the pallor of shame; while a fictitious splendour clothes her hidden breasts.

poems.title: Book IX, 140
poems.author: Claudianus
poems.text: A serving-man stood in the porch of Helicon bearing on his shoulders a brazen-footed stool he had seized, and would not give it to me, tired as I was, to sit on and recite. ‘Therefore ingenious necessity sharpened my wit to deal with the situation.

poems.title: Book IX, 753: On a Crystal enclosing Water
poems.author: Claudianus
poems.text: The snow-white crystal, fashioned by the hand of man, showed the variegated image of the perfect universe, the heaven,?clasping within it the deepvoiced sea.

poems.title: Book IX, 754
poems.author: Claudianus
poems.text: A, tell me, ice, water frozen into stone, who froze thee. B. Boreas. A. And who melted thee? B. The South wind.
